msgs.content:
Draw the requested diagram (reply with one short sentence and a single mermaid block). Choose the clearest Mermaid 12 diagram type. For UML use-case diagrams, use Mermaid 12 syntax beginning with usecase-beta, declare actors with actor ID("Display name"), put use cases inside systemBoundary "System name" ... end, and connect them with -->. Use ..> : include TARGET or ..> : extend TARGET for those relationships, and --|> for generalization.:
MetroPass smart ticketing  
MetroPass is a smart-card and mobile ticketing system for a city metro rail. Any visitor can view the route map, station 
facilities and the fare between two stations without signing in. To buy anything, a passenger must create an account and log 
in, and the system verifies the passenger's mobile number with a one-time password (OTP) whenever a new device is used.  
There are two kinds of passengers: regular passengers and student passengers. Student passengers get a concession fare, 
which requires their institution ID to be verified by the university database once every semester. Passengers can recharge 
their card balance by mobile financial service or debit card; every recharge is processed by an external payment gateway. A 
passenger can also buy a single-journey QR ticket, which follows the same steps as a card recharge but is valid only for that 
day.  
At the gates, the gate reader validates the card at entry and deducts the fare at exit. If the balance is not enough at exit, the 
passenger may top up at the counter before leaving. Passengers can report a lost card and, if they wish, transfer the remaining 
balance to a new card. Station officers can top up cards at the counter and resolve gate complaints. The operations manager 
can change fares and view daily ridership reports, which the system prepares by compiling data from every gate.  
Design a use case diagram based on the above scenario.

<think>
Goal: Create a UML use-case diagram for the MetroPass smart ticketing system.

Constraints:
- Use `usecase-beta` syntax.
- Actors: Visitor, Regular Passenger, Student Passenger, University Database, Payment Gateway, Gate Reader, Station Officer, Operations Manager.
- System Boundary: MetroPass.
- Specific relationships: Include/Extend logic for OTP, fare verification, and top-up processes.

Plausible Approaches:
- Simple list of use cases (too disconnected).
- Grouping by actor (better).
- Using inheritance for Passenger types (most accurate to the prompt).

Refined Structure:
- Actors: Visitor, Passenger (Regular/Student), University DB, Payment Gateway, Gate Reader, Station Officer, Operations Manager.
- Core Use Cases: View Map/Facilities, Create Account, Login (Include: Verify OTP), Recharge Card/Buy QR Ticket (Include: Process Payment), Verify Student ID (Include: University DB), Report Lost Card, Transfer Balance, Top up at Counter, Resolve Complaint, Change Fares, View Ridership Reports.

```mermaid
usecase-beta
    actor "Visitor" as V
    actor "Regular Passenger" as RP
    actor "Student Passenger" as SP
    actor "University Database" as UDB
    actor "Payment Gateway" as PG
    actor "Gate Reader" as GR
    actor "Station Officer" as SO
    actor "Operations Manager" as OM

    RP --|> SP
    SP --|> RP

    V --> (View Route Map)
    V --> (View Station Facilities)
    V --> (View Fare)

    RP --> (Create Account)
    RP --> (Login)
    RP --> (Recharge Card)
    RP --> (Buy QR Ticket)
    RP --> (Report Lost Card)
    RP --> (Transfer Balance)

    SP --> (Verify Student ID)

    (Login) ..> (Verify OTP) : <<include>>
    (Recharge Card) ..> (Process Payment) : <<include>>
    (Buy QR Ticket) ..> (Process Payment) : <<include>>
    (Verify Student ID) -- UDB

    (Process Payment) -- PG
    (View Ridership Reports) -- GR

    SO --> (Top up at Counter)
    SO --> (Resolve Complaint)
    
    OM --> (Change Fares)
    OM --> (View Ridership Reports)

    systemBoundary "MetroPass System" {
        (View Route Map)
        (View Station Facilities)
        (View Fare)
        (Create Account)
        (Login)
        (Verify OTP)
        (Recharge Card)
        (Buy QR Ticket)
        (Process Payment)
        (Verify Student ID)
        (Report Lost Card)
        (Transfer Balance)
        (Top up at Counter)
        (Resolve Complaint)
        (Change Fares)
        (View Ridership Reports)
    }
```

```mermaid
    systemBoundary "MetroPass System" {
        usecase "View Route Map"

        usecase "Create Account"
        usecase "Login"
        usecase "Recharge Card"
        usecase "Buy QR Ticket"

        usecase "Report Lost Card"
        usecase "Transfer Balance"
        usecase "Top up at Counter"

    (Verify Student ID) -- UDB

    (View Ridership Reports) --> GR
    (Top up at Counter) --> SO
    (Resolve Complaint) --> SO
    (Change Fares) --> OM
    (View Ridership Reports) --> OM
```

Find the bug(s) in this code or error. Explain the cause, then give corrected code.

<think>
The error is caused by the use of the `usecase-beta` syntax, which is not a standard or officially supported Mermaid diagram type. Mermaid does not currently have a native `usecase-beta` keyword; use-case diagrams are typically represented using `graph TD` or `flowchart` with specific styling, or by using the `classDiagram` / `sequenceDiagram` types for different logic.

Additionally, the syntax `systemBoundary "Name" { ... }` is not standard Mermaid syntax for defining containers; containers in Mermaid are usually represented as `subgraph`.

To represent a Use Case diagram in Mermaid, the most compatible approach is using a `graph` (flowchart) with nodes representing use cases and actors.

```mermaid
    GR((Gate Reader))
    SO((Station Officer))
    OM((Operations Manager))

    %% System Boundary
    subgraph MetroPass_System [MetroPass System]
        UC1(View Route Map)
        UC2(View Station Facilities)
        UC3(View Fare)
        UC4(Create Account)
        UC5(Login)
        UC6(Verify OTP)

        UC12(Transfer Balance)
        UC13(Top up at Counter)

        UC15(Change Fares)
        UC16(View Ridership Reports)
    end

    %% Visitor Actions

    V --- UC3

    OM --- UC15
    OM --- UC16
```
